sections.heading: The imperfect subjunctive
sections.body: The subjunctive has a past form too. It's easy to build from something you know: take the **ellos form of the preterite**, drop *-ron*, and add *-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran*. Every irregularity of the preterite carries over automatically.

sections.heading: The -se forms
sections.body: There's a second set of endings: *-se, -ses, -se, -semos, -sen* (*hablase, comiese, tuviese*). They mean exactly the same thing. They're common in Spain and in writing; in Latin American speech the *-ra* forms are much more common, so this course uses *-ra* — but recognise *-se* when you read.

sections.heading: When is it used?
sections.body: Anywhere the subjunctive is needed but the trigger is in the past or conditional: *Quería que vinieras* (I wanted you to come), *Me pidió que lo ayudara* (He asked me to help him), in hypothetical *si* clauses (*Si tuviera dinero…*), and in polite requests (*Quisiera un café* — you already know this one!). The next two lessons cover these uses.

examples: Quería que vinieras.
I wanted you to come.
Me pidió que lo ayudara.
He asked me to help him.
Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.
If I had money, I would travel.
Quisiera un café, por favor.
I'd like a coffee, please.
Mis padres querían que estudiara medicina.
My parents wanted me to study medicine.
No creía que fuera verdad.
I didn't think it was true.
Era importante que llegáramos temprano.
It was important for us to arrive early.
Le dije que hiciera la tarea.
I told him to do his homework.
Esperaba que pudieras venir.
I was hoping you could come.
Nos pidió que no dijéramos nada.
She asked us not to say anything.
Buscaba a alguien que supiera francés.
I was looking for someone who knew French.
Si estuviera aquí, te ayudaría.
If I were there, I'd help you.
Me sorprendió que no hubiera nadie.
I was surprised there was nobody there.
Quería que me escribieras.
I wanted you to write to me.
Ojalá viviera cerca del mar.
I wish I lived near the sea.
Si comieran menos, estarían mejor.
If they ate less, they'd feel better.
Si hablaras más despacio, te entendería.
If you spoke more slowly, I'd understand you.
